question: Compare the reaction products when magnesium and sulfur burn in oxygen, and explain how litmus paper identifies their oxide nature.
options: Magnesium burns to form Magnesium Oxide (MgO), which dissolves in water to form Mg(OH)2, turning red litmus blue (Basic
explanation: Magnesium burns to form Magnesium Oxide (MgO), which dissolves in water to form Mg(OH)2, turning red litmus blue (Basic Oxide). Sulfur burns to form Sulfur Dioxide (SO2), forming sulfurous acid in water, turning blue litmus red (Acidic Oxide).

explanation: Physical: 1. Lustre: Metals shiny, non-metals dull. 2. Hardness: Metals hard (except Na, K), non-metals soft/brittle. 3. Malleability: Metals flatten, non-metals break. 4.
